&TERMUX_APP_NAME; was unable to install the bootstrap packages.
&TERMUX_APP_NAME; can only be run as the primary user. \nBootstrap binaries compiled for &TERMUX_APP_NAME; have hardcoded $PREFIX path and cannot be installed under any path other than:\n%1$s.

Android is running &TERMUX_APP_NAME; in the restricted SELinux domain %1$s, which does not allow it to run the programs it installs. Nothing under $PREFIX can be executed while it stays in that domain. \n\nUninstall &TERMUX_APP_NAME; completely and install it again — reinstalling over the top is not enough. The domain is decided when the app is installed and is kept until every app sharing its user id has been removed.%2$s
These installed apps share its user id and target a newer Android version, which is what puts it in that domain:

The glass status bar, dock and keyboard blur a crop of your wallpaper, and this device won\'t hand it over without storage access. Allow it to turn the blur on. Setting a wallpaper from within the launcher works without this permission.

The status bar can show the temperature where you are. It asks for coarse location only — city-level, never a precise fix — and the lookup runs only while the weather widget is switched on. Decline and everything else works exactly the same.

%1$s reads far better with the privileged backend: per-core CPU, detailed memory and the top-process list all come from it. Without it the CPU figure is a best-effort /proc estimate that some ROMs refuse outright, and the widget can end up blank. Set Shizuku up, or turn the widget on anyway and take the unprivileged reading.
